turning-movement.name: Turning movement
turning-movement.summary: Marching around an enemy's flank to threaten his supply lines and line of retreat, forcing him to fight facing the wrong way or to withdraw. It needs speed, secrecy and good scouting.

fixing-force.name: Fixing force
fixing-force.summary: A detachment that holds the enemy's attention and keeps him in place while the main blow lands elsewhere.

column-vs-line.name: March column vs. battle line
column-vs-line.summary: Columns move fast along roads but can barely fire. To fight, a column must first deploy into line, which takes time; a column caught before it deploys is very vulnerable.

dead-ground.name: Using dead ground
dead-ground.summary: Hills, ridges and hollows hide troops moving behind them. Attacking out of ground the enemy cannot see achieves surprise.

massed-artillery.name: Massed artillery
massed-artillery.summary: Guns concentrated in one battery, often on high ground, to pound a single sector, especially troops packed in columns.

shock-cavalry.name: Shock cavalry
shock-cavalry.summary: Heavy cavalry charging in close order at speed, hitting with weight and momentum rather than firepower.

rally-reform.name: Rally and re-form
rally-reform.summary: Bringing troops back into order after a charge or setback, so they can strike again instead of scattering in pursuit.

echelon.name: Echelon attack
echelon.summary: Units advance stepped back one from another, so the line meets the enemy one unit at a time from its strong end while the rest stays back.

oblique-order.name: Oblique order
oblique-order.summary: Frederick the Great's method: mass against one enemy flank and attack in echelon there, while refusing (holding back) the rest of the line.

combined-arms.name: Combined arms
combined-arms.summary: Infantry, cavalry and artillery used together so each covers the others' weaknesses, for example infantry fixing the front while cavalry hits the flank.

pursuit.name: Pursuit
pursuit.summary: Following up a beaten enemy to turn defeat into destruction. Darkness, exhaustion and rearguards limit it.

rearguard.name: Rearguard
rearguard.summary: Fresh, formed troops covering a retreat, slowing the pursuer so the main body can escape.

bait.name: Deliberate weakness (bait)
bait.summary: Leaving a sector apparently weak to lure the enemy into attacking it, drawing his strength away from where the real blow will fall.

strongpoint-defence.name: Defending villages and strongpoints
strongpoint-defence.summary: Stone buildings, walls and streams let a few troops hold off many; villages along a line become small fortresses.

central-position.name: Central position
central-position.summary: Holding the ground between two parts of the enemy's army so they cannot support each other and can be beaten one at a time.

infantry-vs-cavalry.name: Infantry against cavalry
infantry-vs-cavalry.summary: Formed infantry that keeps its nerve (in line or square) can stop a cavalry charge with volleys, leaving the cavalry open to counter-charge.

reserve-commitment.name: Committing the reserve
reserve-commitment.summary: Holding the best troops back and committing them only at the decisive moment, or to restore a crisis.

envelopment.name: Envelopment
envelopment.summary: Attacking an enemy from front and flank or rear at once, so he must fight in two directions or run.

double-envelopment.name: Double envelopment
double-envelopment.summary: Closing on both enemy flanks at once until he is surrounded. Cannae (216 BC) is the archetype.

escape-route.name: Rearguard and escape route
escape-route.summary: A beaten army that keeps order and holds its line of retreat can still get away; one that loses it is destroyed.

decisive-battle.name: Decisive battle
decisive-battle.summary: Aiming not just to win the field but to destroy the enemy army's ability to keep fighting, ending the campaign in a day.

frontal-assault.name: Frontal assault on entrenchments
frontal-assault.summary: Attacking a dug-in enemy head-on across open ground. Rifled muskets, canister and breastworks made it ruinously costly in the American Civil War.

exposed-outpost.name: Exposed advanced position
exposed-outpost.summary: A detachment left in front of the main line can give warning, but if it is caught there it masks the main line's fire as it falls back.

defensive-waiting.name: Waiting on the defensive
defensive-waiting.summary: Holding a strong position and letting the enemy come, because the side that advances on foot against a standing enemy tends to lose.

provoke-attack.name: Provoking the attack
provoke-attack.summary: Moving close enough to hurt a waiting enemy, so that he must either attack on your terms or suffer.

field-obstacles.name: Field obstacles
field-obstacles.summary: Stakes, pits, carts or hedges in front of missile troops break a mounted charge and leave the riders exposed.

narrow-front.name: Crowding on a narrow front
narrow-front.summary: Too many men on too little ground cannot use their numbers; the press itself disorders and kills them.

rear-threat.name: A threat to the rear
rear-threat.summary: A raid or apparent attack behind the line forces a commander to divide his attention or take drastic measures.

defection.name: Pre-arranged defection
defection.summary: Contingents secretly won over before the battle change sides, or stand aside, at the moment that hurts their nominal allies most; the battle is decided before it is fought.

breakout.name: Breakout
breakout.summary: A surrounded force escapes by charging through the enemy rather than away from it, leaving small rearguards to die so the rest can get clear.

feigned-retreat.name: Feigned retreat
feigned-retreat.summary: Troops turn and appear to run so that the enemy breaks ranks to chase them, then face about and strike the disordered pursuers. It needs discipline and drill: a real panic and a pretended one look the same until the turn.

last-stand.name: Last stand
last-stand.summary: A force that cannot escape chooses the strongest ground left to it, often a hill or a wall, and fights until overwhelmed. Usually it buys time for others to get away, or makes a point the survivors and the enemy will remember.

demonstration.name: Demonstration (feint)
demonstration.summary: A visible show of force against one part of the enemy's line, meant to make him reinforce it while the real blow falls elsewhere.

change-of-front.name: Change of front under attack
change-of-front.summary: Turning a linear army to face an enemy who has appeared on its flank. With long lines and drilled step it was slow and risky, and done in haste it crowded the troops into deep, disordered masses.
